thread.title: Dow Climbs as Dips Turn Into Momentum

author: Crystal Kim
title: Dow Climbs as Dips Turn Into Momentum
text:
By Crystal Kim Sept. 27, 2018 12:56 p.m. ET Dig the Rally. Stocks did a U-turn on Thursday, pushing the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 back to where they started the week after a string of down days. The Federal Reserve interest-rate hike was a nonevent , but the rising-rate environment might just gum up the market anyway. In today’s Intraday Update, we…
•…look to historical patterns to divine the direction of the S&P;
•…explain why the market needs to be taken down a notch, on occasion;
•…watch e-commerce juggernaut Amazon.com (AMZN) climb after opening…a store.
Stocks Are Falling Up
Stocks tripped on trade , slid on Fed speak , and fell up . The Dow gained 160 points, or 0.6%, to 26,544.99, the S&P 500 climbed 0.7%, to 2925.53, and the Nasdaq Composite rallied 0.9%, to 8066.47, early Thursday afternoon.
The S&P 500 logged four consecutive declines for the second time this month, but historically down days have fueled rallies, notes Frank Cappelleri , technical analyst at Instinet . In the past five years, the S&P 500 slid for four straight days on 19 different occasions, but it returned an average of 1.23% the following 10 days. During those 10 days, positive returns occurred 100% of the time, with the highest average return of 2.2%.
Tech stocks are helping the S&P rise, but trends might not be on the sector’s side. “Momentum rallied, but its correlation to tech and consumer-discretionary stocks and the overall market has fallen sharply in the last week,” writes Mayank Seksaria , chief macro strategist at Macro Risk Advisors . “The level of correlation remains on the high side. Some rotation at the sector level seems under way below the surface.” He adds that momentum and value volatility have edged up to year-to-date highs.
One momentum-focused strategist is worried about another factor in stock prices: rising rates. “The recent vulnerability of stocks, and especially financials, to selling pressure is partly attributable to the rising rate environment,” says Cliff Drokes , who writes the Momentum Strategies Report .
Stocks could continue their ascent, but Drokes argues the market needs occasional pullbacks, as rising rates cause rate-sensitive securities to sell off. That’s happening now with some bond funds, notably the SPDR Nuveen Bloomberg Barclays Municipal Bond exchange-traded fund (TFI), as investors look to liquidate their income-focused funds, he says.
Expect a hairy start to October, as the number of New York Stock Exchange–listed stocks hitting new lows continues to rise, Drokes adds. There were only 60 new 52-week highs, compared with a whopping 111 new lows, on Wednesday. But again, small dips can provide a bit of thrust for stocks to find their way back up.
Midday Movers
Amazon.com is up 1.7%, to $2,008.32, after opening a new store in New York showcasing highly rated items.
Apple (AAPL) is up 2.1%, to $225.12, after JPMorgan initiated coverage with an Overweight rating.
Carnival (CCL) is down 4.9% after reporting third-quarter earnings. The cruise-ship operator earned $2.36 a share on revenue of $5.84 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $2.32 on revenue of $5.8 billion. For the fourth quarter, the company sees earnings per share of 65 to 69 cents, compared with the 73 cent consensus estimate.
Cameco (CCJ) is up 14.6%, to $11.26, following a favorable ruling from the Tax Court of Canada and an upgrade from Raymond James to Outperform.
Conagra Brands (CAG) is down 6.5%, to $33.72, after reporting first-quarter earnings. The packaged food firm earned 47 cents a share on revenue of $1.83 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 49 cents on revenue of $1.85 billion. For the second quarter, it sees EPS of 57 cents to 60 cents, compared with the 65 cent consensus estimate.
—Teresa Rivas
